title: Disrupting the $15 Trillion Construction Industry with Autonomous Agents: Dr. Sarah Buchner

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 53%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on a vertical-specific RAG system for construction documents with enterprise search and semantic Q&A as the core capability. The core technology is enterprise search over construction corpora and the application vertical is enterprise construction operations. The product is already deployed in production on billions of dollars of construction volume. The talk assumes basic familiarity with RAG but is accessible to a general AI engineer audience. Recorded conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair with a live product demonstration. All evidence anchors are sourced directly from the transcript with grade 'said_in_transcript'.

summary: Dr. Sarah Buchner, Founder & CEO of Trunk Tools, delivered a presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair about disrupting the $15 trillion construction industry with autonomous agents. Construction represents 10% of GDP and is one of the most litigious industries, requiring extensive documentation. A single skyscraper project in New York City involved 3.6 million pages of contracts, blueprints, schedules, RFIs, and other files—a printed stack three times taller than the building itself. This massive unstructured data problem, combined with 10% annual rework costs ($1.5 trillion) caused by data discrepancies, makes construction ideally suited for AI solutions. Trunk Tools built what they call the brain behind construction—a RAG product specifically designed for construction file types that digests and memorizes documentation. On top of this brain, they deploy an army of AI-based agents at a rate of one every 45 days. Their Q&A agent, TrunkText, lets field professionals query construction data via text message or web app, receiving enterprise search results and semantic answers with source citations within seconds. It is already saving field professionals 1-2 hours daily and is used on billions of dollars of construction volume. Buchner demonstrated the agent with a real construction site query about whether door 2103 requires power-actuated hardware, showing how the answer revealed discrepancies in the 3.6 million pages of documentation—mistakes that would be expensive to fix. She also showed examples of the unstructured data challenge, including three-feet-wide tables with dense numbers unusable for humans. Beyond search, Trunk Tools is building agents that automatically generate RFIs to resolve data discrepancies, freeing humans from bureaucratic tasks. Buchner expressed her belief that RAG itself is commoditized, arguing the future lies in vertical agents that solve real-world problems while keeping humans at the center. She estimates $2.5 trillion of the construction industry can be automated with Trunk Tools. The company is actively hiring.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Industry Context
sections.summary: Buchner introduces herself and the construction industry, noting it is the most exciting industry that people consume daily but rarely think about.

sections.title: Scale of Construction Documentation
sections.summary: Describes a NYC skyscraper project using their software with 3.6 million pages of documentation—contracts, blueprints, schedules, RFIs—equivalent to a paper stack three times taller than the building.

sections.title: Industry Challenges and Rework Costs
sections.summary: Explains why construction is prone to errors: massive documentation, highly litigious nature, and integration failures similar to software bugs. Construction is $15T/year with 10% rework ($1.5T) due to data discrepancies.

sections.title: Trunk Tools Solution: The Brain and Agents
sections.summary: Introduces their RAG-based brain behind construction that digests construction-specific file types for a vertical representing 10% of GDP, with an army of AI agents deployed on top.

sections.title: Q&A Agent Demonstration
sections.summary: Demonstrates TrunkText co-pilot handling a real construction query about door 2103 needing power-actuated hardware, delivering enterprise search results and semantic answers via text or web app within seconds. Used on billions of construction volume.

sections.title: Unstructured Data and Discrepancy Resolution
sections.summary: Shows the answer revealed discrepancies in 3.6M pages that would be expensive. Displays three-feet-wide construction tables unusable for humans. Introduces agents that automatically generate RFIs to resolve discrepancies, freeing humans from bureaucracy.

sections.title: Vision: Vertical Agents and Future of RAG
sections.summary: Buchner argues RAG is commoditized and the future is vertical agents solving real-world problems while keeping humans at the center. Invites attendees to join Trunk Tools, which is hiring aggressively.
